name: Kizomba
notes: Kizomba style pack (Doc 04 template; tango's honesty model + salsa's solo-first model). Kizomba is ANGOLAN — born in Luanda in the 1980s, growing out of semba (its parent dance, danced since mid-century) as Angolan musicians absorbed Caribbean zouk (Kassav's influence is widely acknowledged). 'Kizomba' comes from Kimbundu — a word for party/gathering. The pack states this plainly because the style is chronically mislabeled abroad. Two truths shape the design: the GINGA (the grounded, swaying walk) is genuinely trainable solo and is most of the dance; and the close connection cannot be learned by showing — meta.connection_honesty hard-gates every partnered node, exactly like tango's embrace gate. Learn from Angolan and PALOP teachers wherever possible; the etiquette node says so.

seasons.finale: Tell the story out loud on camera: Luanda, semba, the 1980s, what the word kizomba means. Root before step.
Film 60 seconds of the ginga walk — grounded, swaying from the floor up, unhurried.
Film weight transfers riding one slow kizomba track — pauses honored, nothing rushed.
Frame and walk prep done — now attend a first class or social. The connection is learned there.
Go to a kizomba social. Dance a few songs — or sit with the music and watch how little the best dancers do.

attributes.name: Grounded walk L1
attributes.test: 20 slow walks with full weight transfers, knees soft, steps landing whole-foot and silent

attributes.name: Hip sway L1
attributes.test: 20 slow side-to-side transfers with the hips swaying as a RESULT of the transfer, upper body calm

attributes.name: Pause balance L1
attributes.test: hold a mid-step pause 5s on either leg without a wobble — kizomba lives in the pauses

nodes.name: Luanda, Angola — where kizomba is from
checkpoints: kizomba was born in Luanda, Angola in the 1980s — the word comes from Kimbundu, a word for party/gathering
its parent is SEMBA, danced in Angola for decades before; Caribbean zouk (Kassav') shaped the sound
the style is chronically mislabeled abroad — saying 'kizomba is Angolan' correctly is the first step of dancing it

nodes.name: Semba — the parent dance
checkpoints: semba is faster, playful, upright — the umbigada (belly-touch) tradition connects it to older Angolan dances
kizomba slowed semba down as the music slowed down; the walk and the ground feel carry over
watch semba dancers to understand what kizomba relaxed

nodes.name: Learn from the source — Angolan and PALOP teachers
checkpoints: seek Angolan and PALOP (Portuguese-speaking African) teachers first — many teach worldwide and online
derivative branches (urban kiz, fusion) are honest only when they name the Angolan root
when the scene argues about authenticity, the answer is always: go closer to Luanda

nodes.name: The slow pulse — dancing less
checkpoints: kizomba sits slow (roughly 80-100 BPM feel) — the skill is doing LESS, beautifully
the pulse is felt in the knees and the floor, not counted out loud
pauses are music too; the best dancers spend whole phrases nearly still

nodes.name: Kizomba, semba, tarraxinha — the night's flavors
checkpoints: semba tracks: faster, brighter — the walk gets playful
kizomba tracks: the slow rolling core of the night
tarraxinha: slower and more isolated still — a close-connection register learned in person, mentioned here for the ear

nodes.name: The ginga — the kizomba walk
nodes.anchor: most of the dance; a lifetime to make effortless
checkpoints: walk with bent knees, whole-foot steps, weight fully arriving before the next step leaves
the sway is a RESULT: hips answer the transfer, shoulders stay calm
unhurried — the ginga never chases the beat, it strolls beside it
silent feet; the floor is a friend, not a drum
mistakes: swaying from the waist while the legs stay stiff
rushing the transfer — half-arrived steps kill the ground feel

nodes.name: Side transfers & the basic square
checkpoints: side-to-side transfers with the same grounded arrival
the basic square (saída shadow): forward, side, back, side — solo shadow of the partnered pattern
keep the pulse alive through direction changes

nodes.name: Pauses & slow-motion control
checkpoints: stop mid-phrase, settle, breathe, resume — the pause is a full citizen of the dance
half-speed walks: the slower you can go with control, the better you'll follow or lead
let the music decide when; your job is to be stoppable

nodes.name: The honest limit: connection is learned in someone's arms
checkpoints: kizomba's close connection — chest-led, breath-quiet — cannot be taught by video or app; it is learned with real partners, with consent and care, at classes and socials
everything solo in this pack is preparation: the better your ginga, the kinder you are to your first partners
when you're ready, go where the teachers are — ideally Angolan/PALOP-taught rooms

nodes.name: Frame & posture prep (solo)
checkpoints: tall spine over soft knees; the chest is the storyteller in kizomba
walk the ginga with a book-light touch on a wall or chair back: connection without gripping
arms relaxed and heavy — tension is noise in the conversation

nodes.name: The close connection (with a partner)
checkpoints: learned in class and social rooms, with consent as the first step every time
the lead is the chest and the walk, never the arms
this node unlocks by showing up — the app's work here is done

nodes.name: The walking film
checkpoints: one slow track, nothing but ginga, transfers and pauses — filmed
watch it with the sound off: does the body still show the music?
less that looks like more is the whole art

nodes.name: The social
checkpoints: go to a kizomba night — dance, or sit with the music and watch how little the best dancers do
a beginner class before the social is the classic on-ramp
notice whose music is playing and where it came from
